source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.leaves: Blades 3.5–15 × 2–5 cm; historically recognized varieties differ in pubescence, tooth density, petiole length
morphology_documented.flowers: Elongate racemes (4–)6–15 cm with white petals 2.5–6 mm
morphology_documented.habitat: Var. eximia historically associated with Edwards Plateau; var. serotina with more eastern/Red River habitats

source_scope_note: Species-level and key-level traits distinguished; modern secondary traits stay attributed to their own sources.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historical var. eximia often has nearly glabrous leaf underside, ~5 teeth/cm margin and ~12–20 mm petioles on second floral leaf; var. serotina often midrib hair mustache, ~7 teeth/cm, shorter petioles
The 1999 source prints author Ehrend. in extracted text but taxonomic authority is normally Ehrh.; verify against original typography and keep nomenclatural issue open
Wilted foliage can be cyanogenic; flora mentions livestock hazard, not a recommendation for handling
preservation: Additive research only, species JSON and photo/attribution/gallery assets unchanged
